I checked PR #6411 at head a0fccc9 by reading the source. The lost-response and race paths hold up. The pause path does not: a member who is paused can still have an ACP turn started, so this is a fail. I could not run the tests because this machine has no node.

{"result":"fail","summary":"Head a0fccc9d3f233284a9aace3c289a05ad41632236 (PR #6411, base codex/resume-owned-board-claim) was checked from source fetched at that exact SHA via the GitHub API. The tests were read but not run (no node on this host). Lost response holds: a 'queued' pickup receipt is saved before the claim POST. A restarted receiver recovers only with the same signalId plus a held_work offer, and a claim receipt keyed to the lease (claimId + claimedAt) prevents a second prompt. Winner/loser race holds: claimWork only accepts an unclaimed item, and the server returns 409 work_claim_conflict to the loser and to a holder re-claiming; a self-claim enqueues no 'assigned' wake (work-claim-routes.mjs:1501), so acceptClaim cannot start a duplicate. Pause fails. Concrete counterexample: the winner gets the lease and the item is queued, then the owner pauses the member. In claimSignalTurn (bridge.mjs ~522), the only pause gate is room.pickup().status === 'paused'. But room-next.mjs:277-281 sets ifIdle {status:'paused'} only when nothing is addressed to the member. If the member has any open incoming request or addressed work item, ifIdle is absent, so the gate passes. authorized() checks the lease and talk permission but never pause, so host.prompt runs while the member is paused. Even with nothing addressed, a pause that lands during agentReady()/host.session() goes unseen: the re-check after the session (bridge.mjs ~538) is authorized() only, with no pause check. The pause regression test covers only a pause before the claim POST (the server's 423), not a pause after the lease is acquired, so neither path is tested."}
